result.summary: Retains files scheduled for pruning in a persistent BlockManager set rather than a local variable in FlushStateToDisk. When a flush fails before updating the block index database, queued files remain pending and are unlinked after the next successful block index write. If a file pending deletion is reallocated for new block writes in FindNextBlockPos, it is removed from the unlink queue.
result.problem: When a flush that prunes block files fails prior to writing the block index (for instance due to a block file flush error or failed disk space check), the list of files to prune is lost from the local variable. Subsequent successful flushes commit the pruned state to the index but never delete the physical blk and rev files from disk, leaking disk space until ScanAndUnlinkAlreadyPrunedFiles runs on node restart.
evidence: Identified in reviewer ryanofsky's post-merge review of #35714 (#7): block file flush errors and CheckDiskSpace() failures return before the block index write, leaving files unlinked until restart.
Author description notes this unblocks unit testing for the kernel pruning refactor (#35627).
result.card: Validation tracks block and undo files queued for pruning inside BlockManager so they can be deleted across flush retries. Previously, files to prune were held in a local variable in FlushStateToDisk, causing an interrupted flush to mark them pruned in the block index on retry without unlinking the physical files on disk until the next node restart. This resolves an edge case highlighted during review of PR 35714 and unblocks follow-up kernel pruning work in PR 36738 and PR 36739.

risk.why: Incorrect tracking of files to unlink could delete valid block or undo files from disk or corrupt block storage.
